answers.ask: Is this a room you stand in, or an open little outdoor spot?
answers.answer: Un pequeño espacio interior tipo estudio ASMR, minimalista y relajante, con iluminación pastel suave.

answers.ask: Is the tool shop a physical counter in the map, or an on-screen menu?
answers.answer: La tienda será un menú en pantalla moderno y adaptado para PC y celular; así el mapa se mantiene simple y limpio.

answers.ask: One station, or several themed areas you unlock?
answers.answer: Una sola estación principal con los objetos ASMR disponibles desde el inicio; no hacen falta áreas desbloqueables para esta versión pequeña.

scene_prompt: Create a small, minimalist 3D ASMR studio interior with soft pastel lighting and a calm, uncluttered composition. A single central work station holds relaxing breakable materials and objects—soap, kinetic sand, slime, fruit, and soft blocks—arranged neatly on a clean tabletop or display surface, with open space around it for the player. Use gentle visual effects and subtle relaxing particles around the station; no physical shop area.
agent_notes: Simulation: slicing soap, slime and fruit to earn coins and buy better tools is an earn-and-upgrade loop, the clicker end of the genre, with ASMR as theme rather than a second genre. The author's answers close stage B — one main station inside a small minimalist studio, the tool shop is an on-screen menu rather than a counter, and no unlockable areas — which leaves nowhere to walk, so the ASMR bench is the subject and the pastel studio is its setting: set-display, and SET alongside P0 so traversal segmentation and jump-gap checks are skipped while the room still gets built. No preset survived the trim: Incremental Simulator and Physics Sim both lose their shape and nearly all their options here (no storefront, no purchase gates, no circulation between stations), so I emit none and take physics-rig directly for the breakable soap, kinetic sand, slime, fruit and soft blocks whose reactions are the entertainment, plus trigger-task for the cutting station itself. Decided without a user: coins, leaderstats, DataStore and the UI are scripting concerns with no layout geometry, so nothing was emitted for them.

notes: placement mirrored from option 'trigger-task': no siting rule given
